TRIGONOMETRY FORMULA SHEET — 1. BASICS

ANGLES · DEFINITIONS · RECIPROCAL & QUOTIENT · SIGNS

Angle measurement

180°= π radians
1°= π/180 rad = 0.01745 rad
1 radian= 180°/π = 57.3°
θ° to radians= θ × π/180
θ rad to degrees= θ × 180/π
Arc length s= r θ
Sector area A= ½ r² θ

θ must be in radians for arc and sector formulas.

Definitions (point P(x, y), r = √(x² + y²))

sin θ= y/r
cos θ= x/r
tan θ= y/x (x ≠ 0)
cosec θ= r/y (y ≠ 0)
sec θ= r/x (x ≠ 0)
cot θ= x/y (y ≠ 0)

Right-angled triangle

sin θ= perpendicular / hypotenuse
cos θ= base / hypotenuse
tan θ= perpendicular / base
cosec θ= hypotenuse / perpendicular
sec θ= hypotenuse / base
cot θ= base / perpendicular

Memory: Some People Have / Curly Brown Hair / Through Proper Brushing (sin P/H, cos B/H, tan P/B).

Reciprocal & quotient relations

cosec θ= 1/sin θ
sec θ= 1/cos θ
cot θ= 1/tan θ
tan θ= sin θ / cos θ
cot θ= cos θ / sin θ
sin θ · cosec θ= 1
cos θ · sec θ= 1
tan θ · cot θ= 1

Signs in the four quadrants (ASTC: All – Sin – Tan – Cos)

Quadrant I (0°–90°)= all functions positive
Quadrant II (90°–180°)= sin and cosec positive
Quadrant III (180°–270°)= tan and cot positive
Quadrant IV (270°–360°)= cos and sec positive

Full 0°–360° value table, finger trick and ASTC diagram: see the earlier Visual Tricks pages.

COMPOUND & MULTIPLE ANGLES

SUM/DIFFERENCE · DOUBLE · TRIPLE · HALF · POWER REDUCTION · t-SUBSTITUTION

Sum and difference

sin(A ± B)= sin A cos B ± cos A sin B
cos(A ± B)= cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B
tan(A + B)= (tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A tan B)
tan(A − B)= (tan A − tan B)/(1 + tan A tan B)
cot(A + B)= (cot A cot B − 1)/(cot A + cot B)
cot(A − B)= (cot A cot B + 1)/(cot B − cot A)

Double angle

sin 2A= 2 sin A cos A = 2 tan A/(1 + tan²A)
cos 2A= cos²A − sin²A
cos 2A= 2cos²A − 1 = 1 − 2sin²A
cos 2A= (1 − tan²A)/(1 + tan²A)
tan 2A= 2 tan A/(1 − tan²A)
cot 2A= (cot²A − 1)/(2 cot A)

Triple angle

sin 3A= 3 sin A − 4 sin³A
cos 3A= 4 cos³A − 3 cos A
tan 3A= (3 tan A − tan³A)/(1 − 3 tan²A)
cot 3A= (cot³A − 3 cot A)/(3 cot²A − 1)

Memory: sin is 3 − 4 (3 sin − 4 sin³), cos is 4 − 3 (4 cos³ − 3 cos).

sin(A/2)= ±√((1 − cos A)/2)
cos(A/2)= ±√((1 + cos A)/2)
tan(A/2)= (1 − cos A)/sin A = sin A/(1 + cos A)
cot(A/2)= sin A/(1 − cos A)

Sum / difference → product

cos C + cos D= 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2)

Same as 2 sin((C + D)/2) sin((D − C)/2).

Product → sum / difference

2 sin A cos B= sin(A + B) + sin(A − B)
2 cos A sin B= sin(A + B) − sin(A − B)
2 cos A cos B= cos(A + B) + cos(A − B)
2 sin A sin B= cos(A − B) − cos(A + B)

Minimum= −√(a² + b²)

Example: (3 + 2)³ = 27 + 54 + 36 + 8 = 125. More tricks: x + 1/x ladder page.

Quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0

Roots x= (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a
Discriminant D= b² − 4ac
D > 0= two real, distinct roots

D < 0= complex roots (conjugate pair)
Sum of roots= −b/a
Product of roots= c/a

Example: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 → D = 1, roots 3 and 2 (sum 5, product 6).

Graph theory definitions

Branch= one element between two nodes
Node= junction of two or more branches
Loop= closed path
Mesh= loop with no other loop inside
Tree= connects all nodes, no loops
Twig= branch of the tree
Link (chord)= branch not in the tree

Graph theory formulas (B branches, N nodes)

Twigs= N − 1
Links= B − N + 1

Independent KCL

= N − 1

eqns

= B − N + 1

eqns (loops)

Trees of complete graph= NN − 2

Example: N = 6, B = 8 → 5 twigs, 3 links, 5 node and 3 mesh equations.

Exam trick: choose node analysis if N − 1 < B − N + 1, else mesh.

KCL and KVL

KCL= ΣI = 0 at a node (charge conserved)
Sign= entering + , leaving − (current in = current out)
KVL= ΣV = 0 round a loop (energy conserved)
Trick= sum of rises = sum of drops
Single loop= V − IR₁ − IR₂ = 0

Mesh analysis works only for planar circuits; node analysis works for any circuit.

Series, parallel and dividers

Series= Req = R₁ + R₂ + …
Parallel= 1/Req = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …
Two in parallel= R₁R₂/(R₁ + R₂)
Voltage divider= Vx = V Rx/(R₁ + R₂ + …)
Current divider= I₁ = I R₂/(R₁ + R₂)

Larger R gets larger voltage (series); current splits inversely (parallel).

Example: 12 V across 2 Ω + 6 Ω → 9 V on 6 Ω; 10 A into 2 Ω ∥ 3 Ω → 6 A in 2 Ω.

Node voltage method

1. Choose the reference (ground) node.

2. Name the other node voltages.

3. Write KCL at each node.

4. Solve the simultaneous equations.

At node i= Σ (Vᵢ − Vⱼ)/Rᵢⱼ + current sources = 0

Mesh current method

1. Assign clockwise mesh currents.

2. Write KVL in each mesh.

3. Solve.
